en.import.done: Read {conversations} conversations; {candidates} Claude memories added to Pending at zero cost.
en.import.head: Got a Claude / ChatGPT export? Point us at it
en.import.lead: Your export contains memories.json — everything Claude remembers about you. It is already distilled, so it costs no tokens and goes straight into your library. Lose access to the account and it is gone for good; nothing else can rebuild it.
en.import.more: The conversations still need model distillation to become memories — see below.
en.import.placeholder: Path to the unzipped export folder, or conversations.json / memories.json
en.library.empty: Library is empty — start on the Port tab.
en.library.note: The model can call recall_memory for the same results. Exported Markdown / JSONL feeds straight into other memory plugins — they handle "remember from today", this handles "bring the past in".
en.library.placeholder: Ask about something you said before and see if it comes back
en.local.action: Also skim for explicit decisions (free, misses a lot)
en.local.done: The skim only catches explicit patterns like "I decided" or "from now on" — it found {found}. Most real conclusions are implicit; those need model distillation below.
en.mode.balancedDesc: Only money/direction calls, conflicts with existing memories, and AI-inferred items need you. Web-export memories land automatically.
en.mode.head: What lands automatically vs. what you review — your call, changeable anytime:
en.mode.note: This maps to reviewMode in cordis.yml; switching here affects the next port. On the default setting, memories from Claude / ChatGPT web exports land exactly on the auto-store threshold — switch to "Review everything" if you want to be stricter.
en.mode.strictDesc: Nothing is stored without your approval. Safest, but the queue gets long.
en.mode.trustingDesc: Only AI-inferred items and conflicts stop you. Good for porting everything now and reviewing later.
en.model.label: Distill with
en.model.none: (No selectable models right now — the host default will be used.)
en.model.note: Want more depth? A full model pass catches the implicit conclusions rules cannot. The cost: your conversation text is sent to whichever provider you configured in DSH, billed by usage. Porting is a batch job — it can use a different model than your chat, and switching models inside a session does not affect this.
en.panel.subtitle: Accounts come and go. Your memory shouldn't.
en.panel.title: Memory Porter
en.queue.empty: Queue is empty — either you have reviewed everything, or nothing has been ported yet.
en.queue.note: Sorted so the ones most worth a look come first. Each is tagged with why it needs you. Discarded items never come back.
en.reason.human-conflict: Review · conflicts with an existing memory
en.reason.human-user-choice: Review · you chose to review everything
en.report.blocked: {count} were rejected because they did not match the source text — evidence must appear verbatim in what you actually said; paraphrase never counts.
en.report.fromAssistant: {count} more were backed by the AI's restatement rather than your own words — all pushed to Pending, never stored automatically.
en.report.line: Done (via {model}): {candidates} candidates from {conversations} conversations — {accepted} stored automatically, {pending} awaiting your review.
en.run.progress: Porting {done} / {total} chunks — the model reads each segment in turn, so this can take minutes with many conversations. Keep the panel open.
